'''Ichishi-no-Nagaochi''' (''ichishi no nagaochi''{{Sfn|Ichishi-no-Nagaochi (Ancient Clans)|2010}}; dates of birth and death unknown) was a {{ill|Kofun-period|ja|古墳時代}} {{ill|gōzoku|ja|豪族}} transmitted in the ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}'' and one of the '''{{ill|Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|倭国造}}'''. Also called '''Ichishi-no-Nagaochi-no-Sukune'''.

He is the distant ancestor of the Yamato-no-Atai (Yamato clan), and is known for the origin tale of {{ill|Yamato-no-Ōkunitama-no-Kami|ja|倭大国魂神}} (the enshrined deity of {{ill|Ōyamato Shrine|ja|大和神社}} in {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|lt=Tenri City}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}). He does not appear in the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}}''.

== Records ==
[[File:Oyamato-jinja, haiden.jpg|thumb|200px|right|{{ill|Ōyamato Shrine|ja|大和神社}} ({{ill|Tenri, Nara|ja|天理市|lt=Tenri City}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]]
According to the ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}'', {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}} year 7, eighth month, seventh day, three people — Yamatototohi-Asaji-hara-Mawaka-hime ({{ill|Yamato-Totohi-Momoso-hime-no-Mikoto|ja|倭迹迹日百襲姫命}}), {{ill|Ōmizukuchi-no-Sukune|ja|大水口宿禰}} (distant ancestor of the {{ill|Hozumi-no-Omi|ja|穂積氏|lt=Hozumi-no-Omi}}), and {{ill|Ise-no-Omi-no-Kimi|ja|伊勢麻績君}} — shared a dream in which they were divinely instructed that if {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|lt=Ōtataneko-no-Mikoto}} and Ichishi-no-Nagaochi were appointed as the priests of {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主|lt=Ōmononushi-no-Kami}} (later the deity of {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|ja|大神神社}}) and Yamato-no-Ōkunitama-no-Kami (later the deity of {{ill|Ōyamato Shrine|ja|大和神社}}) respectively, the realm would surely become peaceful. They reported this to the emperor. Accordingly, on the 8th day of the 11th month of Sujin year 7, Ōtataneko and Nagaochi were ordered to perform the worship as the dream foretold, the plague subsided, and the realm became calm.{{Sfn|Ichishi-no-Nagaochi (Ancient Clans)|2010}} (The same account appears in an "alternative" tradition under {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇}} year 25, third month.)

The same book, Emperor Suinin year 3, third month, in an "alternative" tradition, records that he was ordered by the emperor — together with Ōtomonushi (ancestor of the {{ill|Miwa-no-Kimi|ja|大神氏|lt=Miwa-no-Kimi}}; {{ill|Ōmiwa Ōtomonushi|ja|大三輪大友主}}) — to go to {{ill|Harima|ja|播磨国|lt=Harima}} to interrogate the Silla prince {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|アメノヒボコ|lt=Amenohiboko|lt_ja=天日槍}}, who had come from {{ill|Silla|ja|新羅}}.{{Sfn|Ichishi-no-Nagaochi (Ancient Clans)|2010}}

Further, the ''Nihon Shoki'', Emperor Suinin year 7, seventh month, seventh day, records that he was ordered to bring back {{ill|Nomi-no-Sukune|ja|野見宿禰}} of {{ill|Izumo Province|ja|出雲国}} to be a wrestling opponent for {{ill|Taima-no-Kuehaya|ja|当麻蹶速}}.{{Sfn|Ichishi-no-Nagaochi (Ancient Clans)|2010}}

== Analysis ==
The name element "Ichishi" is identified with a place name in {{ill|Tōchi District, Yamato|ja|十市郡|lt=Tōchi District}}, {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|大和国}} (around Ikenouchi, {{ill|Sakurai, Nara|ja|桜井市|lt=Sakurai City}}, Nara Prefecture).{{Sfn|Ichishi-no-Nagaochi (Kokushi)}}{{Sfn|Ichishi-no-Nagaochi (Ancient Clans)|2010}}
